summary.text: 国 means “country” or “nation.” It is a simplified form of 國, whose traditional structure combines 囗, marking territory, with 或 as a sound element. In 国, 玉 occupies 或’s position; the history of that replacement is unclear.

formation.text: The traditional graph 國 is phonosemantic: 囗 contributes the territory meaning, and 或 supplies a sound cue. The curated Western Zhou bronze-style image shows an angular inner element within an enclosure; it is a modern redraw illustrating the structure, not an artifact or a sequence of forms. The current graph 国 has 玉 in place of 或, but the reason and pathway for this graphic change are unclear.

components.text: In 國, 囗 marks a boundary or territory. Some Warring States forms are reported with 匚 or 𠃊 in the same boundary-marker role. This component belongs to 國, the traditional graph from which 国 is simplified.
In 國, 或 is the phonetic element, but its original depicted referent is not known. 国 has 玉 in the corresponding inner position; the history of this substitution is unclear.

sound_limitation.text: The reconstructions support a sound relationship between 或 and 國 but do not identify 或’s original depicted referent. Modern readings alone do not prove its role in 國.

sound.text: In Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese reconstructions, 國 *kʷɯːɡ and 或 *ɡʷɯːɡ are similar but differ in their initial consonant. These are reconstructed forms, not direct records of ancient speech.

components.text: 玉 is the visible inner element in 国, occupying the position of 或 in 國. It is a graphic replacement; the evidence does not show when or why this substitution arose.

history.text: A modern redraw of a Western Zhou bronze-script-style form shows an angular inner element inside an enclosure. It illustrates the reported structure of 國, not an artifact or a proven sequence of graphic stages.

國 with 囗 is reported in Western Zhou bronze inscriptions for “country/state.” Warring States forms may vary the boundary marker; later bamboo slips and Han silk manuscripts also use 國 with this meaning. These examples document usage but do not establish a sequence of graphic stages or later meanings.

A Han-dynasty dictionary account analyzes 國 as 囗 plus 或 and glosses it as 邦. The proposed reading of 或 as “country” in the He zun inscription is disputed; another interpretation takes it as 域, “territory.”
国 is reported as simplified from 國, with 玉 in the position of 或, and as the Japanese shinjitai corresponding to 國. The precise pathway and date of this graphic change are unclear.

uncertainties.text: The secure earliest attestation of the word meaning “country/state” remains unsettled: the proposed He zun reading of 或 as 國 is disputed, and the cited research does not include a complete inscription survey.
A dated semantic path from boundary or territory to polity, and the chronology of later senses such as “nation-state,” are not established.
The evidence reports the replacement 或 → 玉 but does not establish its precise historical pathway or why 玉 was selected.

senses.period: Western Zhou inscriptions reported; exact earliest attestation unresolved
senses.text: Western Zhou bronze inscriptions are reported to use 國 for “country/state.” This supports the sense in that period, though the disputed He zun reading of 或 leaves the word’s earliest attestation unsettled.
The character is currently used for “nation” and “country.” The evidence does not date how this range developed from the older country/state sense.

limitations.text: The evidence does not establish a dated semantic transition from territory or state to the current range “nation, country, nation-state.”

items.caption: A Western Zhou bronze-script style form of 國 places an angular inner element within a surrounding boundary. The enclosing 囗 marks territory, while the inner 或 serves as the phonetic element.
items.alt: A thick, rounded rectangular enclosure around an angular inner form with several short strokes and a loop.
